stories.title: China / Taiwan
stories.detail: Above its own baseline: 11 headlines against a normal of 13.7, and new language today (blockade). That is a change, not just continuing coverage.
stories.why: Low frequency, very high severity. A genuine blockade or invasion scenario is the largest single tail risk in the gold market, because it would be a global supply-chain and reserve-currency event simultaneously.
stories.counterweight: Routine incursions and drills are so frequent they carry almost no information. Gold ignores them, correctly.
stories.duration: Drills: nothing. A real blockade: a regime change in gold pricing, not a spike.
stories.spoken_why: Routine drills mean nothing, but a genuine blockade would be the largest single risk in this market.
stories.read: Broadly consistent, though US 10-year yield, Gold, WTI crude are not playing along. One asset out of line is usually its own story; several is a reason to doubt the read.

stories.title: Trade and tariffs
stories.detail: Above its own baseline: 3 headlines against a normal of 0.8. That is a change, not just continuing coverage.
stories.why: Indirect but real. Tariffs are an inflation impulse and a growth drag at once, which is the hardest combination for the Fed and therefore raises uncertainty about the rate path.
stories.counterweight: Also dollar-positive in the short run, which works against gold. The net effect is genuinely ambiguous and often small.
stories.duration: Weeks, when it changes the inflation outlook. Announcement headlines alone rarely stick.
stories.spoken_why: Tariffs raise prices and slow growth at the same time, which is the hardest combination for the Federal Reserve to answer.
stories.read: Broadly consistent, though Gold, WTI crude are not playing along. One asset out of line is usually its own story; several is a reason to doubt the read.

stories.title: Russia / Ukraine / NATO
stories.detail: 11 headlines against a normal of 20.8. Nothing that stands out from its own background.
stories.why: Two channels: haven demand, and the structural one - sanctions on Russian reserves in 2022 taught central banks that dollar reserves can be frozen, which is a large part of why official-sector gold buying has been so persistent since.
stories.counterweight: Day-to-day headlines are largely priced. The structural bid shows up in central bank demand data, not in a day's price action.
stories.duration: Headlines: days. The reserve-diversification effect: years, and it is arguably the single biggest reason gold has re-rated.
stories.spoken_why: The day to day headlines are priced, but sanctions on reserves are why central banks keep buying gold.
stories.read: Broadly consistent, though Gold, Silver, Copper and 1 others are not playing along. One asset out of line is usually its own story; several is a reason to doubt the read.

stories.title: US / Israel – Iran
stories.detail: Coverage is below its own normal and carrying de-escalation language. Any risk premium here should be fading.
stories.why: The one flashpoint that hits gold through every channel at once. Safe-haven bid on the headline, Treasuries bid so nominal and real yields fall, and - uniquely - a credible threat to the Strait of Hormuz spikes crude, which lifts inflation expectations. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil passes through that strait.
stories.counterweight: The dollar is also a haven, so risk-off bids the dollar too and cancels part of gold's gain. This is why some escalation days produce a far smaller gold move than the headlines imply.
stories.duration: Days. Gold spikes on the exchange of fire and gives most of it back within a week unless the oil disruption is real and sustained, because only then does it reach the Fed's reaction function.

headlines.summary: For decades, these bases allowed the US to wage faraway wars. Now, Iran has changed that calculation.

headlines.title: Iran open to deal if US ‘refrains from excessive demands’, says Ghalibaf
headlines.summary: Iran’s chief negotiator says Iran is open to a deal if the US refrains from creating distrust and excessive demands.

geo.caveat: Each flashpoint is measured against its own trailing 30-day median, so a long-running conflict does not sit at maximum forever. This measures how loud a story is relative to its own normal - not what will happen.

profile.name: Initial Jobless Claims
profile.what: New unemployment benefit filings in the prior week. Released every Thursday at 13:30 UK.
profile.why_gold: The highest-frequency labour signal available. Individually minor, but a trend of rising claims shifts the whole rate narrative.
profile.watch: The four-week moving average rather than the weekly print, and continuing claims for whether people are finding new work.
profile.gotchas: Distorted by holidays, weather and state-level administrative quirks. One bad week means nothing.

profile.name: FOMC Member Speaks
profile.what: Remarks from a regional Fed president or governor.
profile.why_gold: Mostly background, but a known hawk turning dovish - or the reverse - is a genuine signal, and voting members matter more than non-voters.
profile.watch: Whether the speaker votes this year, and whether they are departing from their usual stance.
profile.gotchas: Several speakers a day is normal and almost always noise. Treat as background unless the tone genuinely shifts.
